question: What is the main goal of conducting a situation analysis in community health?

options.A: To immediately punish health workers who fail to meet targets
options.B: To write a long report that will be kept inside a filing cabinet
options.C: To understand current health status and local resources before planning
options.D: To distribute free medications without consulting community leaders

explanation: A situation analysis acts as a baseline study to reveal community needs and available resources so that nurses can plan effective care. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to start a health program without doing a situation analysis first?

options.A: Community members will refuse to ever speak to healthcare workers
options.B: The government will refuse to disburse salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: Local pharmacy shops will immediately report the clinic to the police
options.D: The program might target problems the community does not consider important

explanation: Skipping situation analysis often leads to wasted resources because interventions fail to address the actual priorities of the local population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h1)

question: How does a situation analysis help with resource allocation?

options.A: By allowing private clinics to buy government drugs cheaply
options.B: By ensuring every single village gets the exact same amount of money
options.C: By hiding medical supplies from the Ministry of Health
options.D: By directing scarce supplies to areas with the greatest need

explanation: Because health resources are always limited, data from a situation analysis ensures supplies go where disease burdens are highest. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h2)

question: What does setting a baseline mean in the context of community health planning?

options.A: Calculating the exact cost of building a fence around the clinic
options.B: Establishing the starting measurements to evaluate future progress
options.C: Writing down the names of all nurses working in the primary health center
options.D: Listing the minimum amount of salary a community health worker accepts

explanation: A baseline gives you initial numbers, like immunization coverage rates, so you can measure improvement after your program runs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following belongs to the epidemiological component of a health profile?

options.A: Prevalence of malaria and malnutrition rates
options.B: Total number of children enrolled in primary school
options.C: Condition of roads leading to the primary health center
options.D: Average monthly income of market women

explanation: Epidemiology looks at disease patterns, illness rates, and health conditions affecting the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why must a community health profile include data on the physical environment, such as water sources?

options.A: Nurses are required by law to test the pH of every borehole in the state
options.B: Water sources directly influence the spread of waterborne infections like cholera
options.C: Environmental data determines the retirement age of community leaders
options.D: The Ministry of Water Resources pays bonuses to clinics that report rain

explanation: Unsafe drinking water is a major root cause of many infectious diseases managed at primary health care facilities. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is a key informant interview?

options.A: A rigid questionnaire filled out by every single child in the village
options.B: A discussion with community leaders who possess deep local knowledge
options.C: A secret examination taken by nursing students before clinical posting
options.D: A laboratory test used to diagnose stubborn bacterial infections

explanation: Key informants include respected local figures like elders or teachers who can explain community habits and history. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h4)

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why mothers refuse to bring babies for routine immunization. Which data collection method is best suited for this?

options.A: Measuring the height and weight of newborn babies
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccines in the clinic fridge
options.C: Counting the number of cars passing through the main highway
options.D: Focus group discussions with local nursing mothers

explanation: Focus group discussions allow mothers to openly share their personal beliefs, fears, and cultural concerns regarding immunization. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the difference between a felt need and a real need in community health?

options.A: A felt need is what the community asks for, while a real need is what data shows they lack
options.B: A felt need can be solved with money, while a real need requires federal approval
options.C: A felt need is written in hospital books, while a real need is spoken secretly
options.D: A felt need affects children, while a real need only affects elderly men

explanation: Communities often request things like a big hospital building, when data shows their actual greatest need is clean drinking water to stop cholera. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h5)

question: A health team has money to tackle only one issue. They choose malaria because it kills more children in the village than any other disease. Which prioritization criterion are they using?
explanation: Choosing a problem because it affects many people (magnitude) and causes death (severity) is the core of healthcare prioritization. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which group of people should be involved during a community health situation analysis?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting local tourist attractions
options.C: Local stakeholders like traditional leaders and women's groups
options.D: Only doctors from the federal capital city

explanation: True community health relies on involving local leaders and residents who understand their environment and hold social influence. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is community participation critical after a health plan has been created?

options.A: It prevents the local government from taxing the primary health center
options.B: It creates a sense of ownership so the community maintains the project
options.C: It ensures that health workers receive extra allowances from donors
options.D: It allows nurses to transfer all their daily workload to local volunteers

explanation: When communities participate in identifying and planning solutions, they protect and sustain the project long after external funding ends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the final step after completing a community situation analysis?

options.A: Closing down the primary health center for renovations
options.B: Translating the findings into an actionable health plan
options.C: Waiting for another NGO to come and do the work
options.D: Destroying all survey papers to protect patient privacy

explanation: The entire purpose of gathering and analyzing situation data is to guide practical healthcare planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to use data showing high rates of childhood malnutrition in a health plan?

options.A: Ignoring the data and focusing only on building a new staff office
options.B: Starting regular growth monitoring sessions at the primary health center
options.C: Setting up nutrition education classes using affordable local foods
options.D: Collaborating with agricultural extension workers to promote backyard gardens

explanation: A health plan must directly respond to identified problems like malnutrition, rather than spending resources on unrelated administrative projects. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)
